**Verdict on the proposed answer: 71 is very likely correct, but the solution does not prove that it is achieved.**

**Reformulation (correct).** The condition says $V(M_i)$ is independent in $H_{i+1}$. Reading the parts from $M_t$ back to $M_1$, each step adds a 2-matching on 4 vertices that span no edges of the graph built so far. Equivalently, in the complement $K_{19}$, each step removes a perfect matching of a $K_4$.

**Upper bound (correct).** Track one vertex $v$ and its degree $d$ in $H$. Each time $v$ participates, its degree rises by exactly 1. Participation needs three pairwise non-adjacent non-neighbours of $v$, so $d \le 14$ beforehand. Suppose $v$ reaches degree 15 at some step with partners $u,a,b$ and remaining non-neighbour $c$. The matched pair $\{a,b\}$ is then adjacent, so $\{a,b,c\}$ is never independent again and $v$ cannot participate further. Hence each vertex participates at most 15 times. Since each part uses 4 vertex-participations,
$$4t \le 19 \cdot 15 = 285 \implies t \le 71.$$
The proposed proof of the degree-3 invariant in the complement is also valid, and it gives the same bound.

This matches the case $n=19$, which also has slack 1, so 71 is plausible.

The upper bound is rigorous, and the tight small cases make 71 likely correct. The missing construction is a real gap in the write-up, not a flaw in the value.
